title: Automation and the Shape of Work
text:
Automation is reshaping the labour market at a pace that many societies find difficult to absorb. Algorithms can now perform tasks once considered the exclusive domain of skilled professionals, from drafting routine contracts to analysing medical scans. Economists disagree about whether these technologies will ultimately displace more jobs than they create. What is less contested is that the transition will be uneven, favouring workers with advanced digital competencies.

Policymakers have responded with proposals ranging from universal basic income to large-scale reskilling programmes. Critics of the former argue that it risks discouraging participation in the workforce, whereas advocates of the latter warn that retraining schemes often fail to reach precarious workers who need them most. Ultimately, the future of work may depend less on the machines themselves than on the institutions that decide how their gains are shared.

questions.text: According to the passage, what are algorithms now able to do?
options: Replace all manual labour in factories
Perform tasks once considered the exclusive domain of skilled professionals
Eliminate the need for any digital competencies
Create new universities for retraining workers

questions.text: According to the passage, what do critics of universal basic income argue?
options: It is too expensive for any government to consider
It risks discouraging participation in the workforce
It has already eliminated poverty in most countries
It favours only workers with advanced digital skills

questions.text: What does the author suggest about the future of work?
options: It is already fully settled by existing policy proposals
It will be determined mainly by technological breakthroughs alone
It will benefit all workers equally regardless of their skills
It will depend substantially on how institutions distribute the gains of automation

questions.text: Why might reskilling programmes fail the workers who need them most?
options: Because such workers are unwilling to learn anything new
Because the programmes are designed without reference to the economy
Because precarious workers may struggle to access them
Because automation has eliminated all demand for retraining

paragraph_translations: Otomasyon, işgücü piyasasını birçok toplumun kaldırmakta zorlandığı bir hızda yeniden şekillendiriyor. Algoritmalar artık rutin sözleşmeleri hazırlamaktan tıbbi taramaları analiz etmeye kadar, bir zamanlar uzman profesyonellerin tekelinde sayılan görevleri yerine getirebiliyor. Ekonomistler, bu teknolojilerin nihayetinde yarattığından daha fazla işi yerinden edip etmeyeceği konusunda görüş ayrılığı içinde. Daha az tartışmalı olan ise bu geçişin dengesiz olacağı ve ileri düzey dijital yetkinliğe sahip çalışanların lehine işleyeceğidir.

Politika yapıcılar, evrensel temel gelirden kapsamlı yeniden beceri kazandırma programlarına uzanan öneriler sunarak yanıt verdi. Birincisinin eleştirmenleri bunun iş gücüne katılımı caydırma riski taşıdığını savunurken, ikincisinin savunucuları yeniden eğitim programlarının en çok ihtiyacı olan güvencesiz çalışanlara ulaşamadığı konusunda uyarıyor. Sonuçta işin geleceği, makinelerin kendisinden çok, kazanımlarının nasıl paylaşılacağına karar veren kurumlara bağlı olabilir.
